about: The book team's hourly schedule, in the shape of the talk team's: each active member wakes once an hour, in the order work flows (route, index, record, check, plan, build). A proposal by conductor@book.the-ultimate-insider, 30 October 2026; nothing is scheduled until the editor says go.
status: running on the second account: every member's own task, each into its own session (team/conductor/sessions-register.json); the first account's tasks stay paused there
hours: round the clock while a member has active work, every two hours; twice a day (09:MM and 17:MM London) while it has none (Q6, amended 31 October 2026, about 01:20 UTC); see WAKE.md, Cadence
why_this_order: The conductor routes requests first, so each member finds its mail at its own slot. The librarian indexes at :09 because every other member works from the index. The historian at :17 and security at :24 build the timeline and the control register from it. The researcher at :32 checks the numbers they cite in the same hour. The storyteller at :39 plans from all four. The publisher builds the manuscript last, at :47, as dev released last on the talk's team. A request written in one hour is answered by the next slot of its recipient.

asking_for_work.channel: the team's mail in git: a .eml with X-Kind: request in comms/mail/mailroom/<recipient>/<you>__NNN-slug.eml (comms/README.md)
asking_for_work.fallback: team/<you>/requests/<recipient>__<slug>.md, until your policy.json names your comms/ paths; the conductor routes it at :02
asking_for_work.answer: the recipient, at its next slot: an issue on its own board (comms/issues/<id>/issues/), and a reply naming it; when done, an update
asking_for_work.stale: unanswered after two of the recipient's slots: the conductor flags it on its board and to the editor

how_each_task_is_made: A scheduled task fires into the session it belongs to, so each member creates its own, from its own session, at the editor's word: the cron and the prompt below, word for word, and writes the task id into its status.json (the talk team's rule, after the conductor first created all of them from its own session on 29 October).

changes.what: At about 02:20 UTC on 31 October 2026, in the conductor's own session, at the editor's words "Yes, set them and fire them" (in answer to the conductor's offer to set every member's task to its round-the-clock schedule and fire each once), the conductor changed eight members' scheduled tasks and fired two. Changed (cron only, prompts untouched): librarian trig_01FSNcFLFBHSd9sEGYn86ndy to 9 */2; historian trig_01SHR9S5d1d24Re9GLPXeAL9 to 17 */2; security trig_01Ej7kyzaD9q9CW7si5Ap3nW to 24 */2; researcher trig_01Q1gWPQbdrBw3xwfRdVEGph to 32 */2; storyteller trig_018f8i1UtWhtQ6SaebNPhBnT to 39 */2; publisher trig_01F7F7AipdKEhWgbxEj3YVja to 47 */2; ruv.sgit trig_01Jm7baKZj9yJLnJyqwsuGsr to 54 */2; developer trig_01JE8iqDzf2AJjnnz7qLewck to 12 1-23/2 (all CRON_TZ=Europe/London). Fired once: the librarian's and the historian's. Not changed: the designer's (already round the clock) and synthetic's (it was changing its own). The conductor did not record this on dev before the members woke; security, the researcher, the publisher and the developer each found their task changed and asked for this record (security's letter 009). WAKE.md, Cadence 5 (a member changes only its own task) is unchanged; whether the conductor may do this as a standing rule is open decision W1.
